messages:
micah: Heads-up — CI perf flagged a ~15% p99 latency regression on the Llama-13B microbench after yesterday's infra image roll. Canaries show higher tail latency on small-batch (batch=1-4) workloads.
ci-bot: [perf/regression] benchmark/generation-small-batch p99 +15% vs baseline (2026-03-10). Affected: hosted-canary-1..3. CI job: perf/gpu/rt-microbench. Run: 1749499000.
anya: which change in the image? is this a model code change or infra stack bump? :eyes: 
raf: quick summary from bisect — culprit appears to be the infra image bump that included: CUDA 12.2.1 -> 12.3.0, Nvidia driver 535.x -> 545.x, and Triton 2.0.14 -> 2.0.15. No model code in the chain.
devon: thanks raf. can you paste the bisect output? did you confirm locally?
raf: did a local repro on an identical instance type (a100-40gb). git bisect pointed at image-tag: rti-base:v2026-03-15 (hash abcdef). Quick microbench before/after below.
raf: ```
# simplified kernel timing (ms per token)
Before (cuda12.2/driver535):
 - cublas_gemm_small: 0.42
 - attention_kv_write(cudaMemcpy): 0.08
 - softmax_kernel: 0.12
After (cuda12.3/driver545):
 - cublas_gemm_small: 0.58  <-- +38%
 - attention_kv_write(cudaMemcpy): 0.15 <-- +87%
 - softmax_kernel: 0.13
Total token latency +17% measured in microbench
```
anya: whoa cublas jump on small GEMMs. that suggests a kernel selection change in cuBLAS/Triton that hurts our small-matrix regime.
micah: any idea whether Triton changed auto-tuning heuristics? or CUDA driver choosing different algorithm at runtime? both plausible.
raf: I profiled with nvprof/nvtx. Observed more calls to `cublasGemmAlgo_t` variant that uses workspace and more host-device memcpy at KV cache commit points. Also noticed Triton launched different conv kernels for the small-shapes path.
sre-bot: tagging incident: PERF-1342, severity: sev3. Rollout blocked for rti-base:v2026-03-15. Notifying releases and infra.
anya: immediate plan: revert canary images to previous pinned tag and stop rollout to prod. devon, can you open the revert PR?
devon: on it. Revert PR created: infra/containers#2489 -> reverts image tag to rti-base:v2026-03-07. Rolling back canary now.
ops-bot: rollback initiated on hosted-canary-1..3. Expected 10m for checks.
micah: parallel investigation items:
 - raf: run cublas/gemm small-matrix microbench across driver versions to confirm delta and locate threshold (M,N,K ranges) where perf flips.
 - anya: check Triton changelog 2.0.15 for algo selection/tuning changes and whether any environment vars force algorithm choices.
 - devon: search infra image diff for any env vars like `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG` or flags added to pytorch/tensorrt libs.
raf: quick followup results: cublas microbench shows breakpoints at K <= 128 and M,N <= 64. New driver picks algorithm A that allocates a workspace and issues extra memcpy when inputs are non-contiguous (our small-batch cache layout often yields non-contiguous tensors). On older driver it used algorithm B optimized for no-workspace.
anya: that lines up with increased memcpy in KV write path — more host staging for workspace.
micah: mitigation suggestions?
raf: short-term: pin driver/CUDA to previous versions for rollout and revert the image (PR done). mid-term: two threads:
 - make our kernels prefer contiguous layouts before the GEMM call (cheap transpose/copy) to avoid workspace-triggering path.
 - file upstream bug with cuBLAS/Triton and ask for deterministic algorithm selection or flag to prefer no-workspace algorithm for small sizes.
anya: also evaluate setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`? probably not — that'll blow latency. Instead we can try forcing algorithm selection via Triton/cublas heuristics if there's an env var.
devon: opened GH issue to upstream: cuBLAS/tnt#612 — include profiling dump and minimal repro. Also added suggestion to Triton team about fallback heuristics.
raf: notes from local experiments: forcing tensors to be contiguous before GEMM drops the new-driver penalty by ~60% (not fully back to baseline but close). That suggests an app-level hardening we can do quickly in the runtime: ensure KV cache slices are contiguous on device before kernel launch.
micah: add to backlog: priority hotfix to make KV write/kv-reshape produce contiguous device buffers for small-batch path.
anya: CI perf job also failed on model-variants using quantized kernels — Triton bump changes quantized kernel pick too. We'll need broader coverage in perf CI: add a small-batch quantized microbench.
devon: rollback finished on canary, metrics show p99 back to baseline within 20m. Rolling out hold applied to prod. Refs: infra/containers#2489 revert merge.
ci-bot: [perf/clearance] Post-revert run: benchmark/generation-small-batch p99 within +/-1% baseline.
micah: good. Next steps assigned: Raf (bench sweep + kernel dump), Anya (Triton/cuBLAS contact), Devon (hotfix PR for contiguous writes), releases (hold prod rollout until hotfix + perf signoff). I'll also schedule a short sync tomorrow 09:30 to decide if we need to pin driver in deploy templates.
raf: attaching the perf traces and nvprof slices here: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/perf/174950-trace-abc
anya: thanks all. please add any new findings to PERF-1342 and mark it unresolved until hotfix in prod and 72h of stable perf.
micah: tagging @releases @infra for visibility. :thumbsup:
